result.title: DeDiCa: A Scalable Deconfounding Discrete Causal Generative Model
result.summary: We introduce DeDiCa, a practical framework for efficient causal inference with discrete variables and hidden confounding that revisits classical probabilistic modeling through a tensorized parameterization of causal Bayesian networks, enabling tractable inference. Given a causal graph, DeDiCa is trained once on observational data by maximum likelihood, exactly marginalizing over hidden confounders, and can then estimate any (proxy-)identifiable interventional query. Despite this deliberately simple parameterization, DeDiCa matches state-of-the-art neural causal generative models in ATE estimation, while supporting memory-efficient CPU training and exact interventional inference in milliseconds. Compared with causal foundation models, DeDiCa scales more effectively with additional observational samples and achieves competitive accuracy at substantially lower inference time and memory. DeDiCa provides a tractable, accurate, and scalable approach to causal inference in discrete settings with hidden confounding.

AI.brief_summary: DeDiCa 用张量化参数化的离散因果贝叶斯网络建模含隐藏混杂的数据，一次最大似然训练后即可精确地对隐变量边缘化，并回答可识别的干预查询，在 ATE 估计上达到神经因果生成模型的水平且推理更快更省内存。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 VLM/latent 视觉推理无直接关联，但其对离散隐变量做精确干预推断的框架，可能可供核查用于诊断 latent 推理状态的因果作用与贡献分配；联系的可行性尚需阅读原文确认。
